source: TSTD project (TA 7305-CAM), "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំពោត" (Corn Cultivation Technical Manual), Section 1: Land preparation and bed-making, May 2012
text:
Before planting corn, the field must be cleared of weeds and crop debris left over from the previous crop. Plow the field while the soil still holds enough moisture, then let it dry for 10-15 days before further work. Drainage/irrigation ditches around the plot should be dug 10-20 cm wide.

Raised beds for planting corn can be made either by hand tools (hoe) or with a small tractor/tiller. When making beds by hand: a bed 1 meter wide should be left with a drainage gap roughly every 50 meters because water tends to pool along the length of a continuous bed; furrow depth should be 20-30 cm in the dry season and 30-50 cm in the rainy season. Fertilizer (base compost/manure) is spread evenly across the width of the bed and then covered over with a layer of soil before planting.

When making beds using a hand tiller/small tractor, the machine can create a single row or double row bed. A single-row bed is about 3.5 m wide (3-4 rows spaced ~3.5m), and a double-row bed is about 4.5 m wide, made within one pass of the machine. Farmers should also leave cross-drains (perpendicular channels) roughly every 20-30 meters along the bed system, tying into the surrounding irrigation ditches, so that water does not pool inside the beds.
